title: Deployment trigger synthesizer for multi‑SLO orchestration
creator: Aisha Banerjee
description:
Goal: implement a signal synthesis layer ("trigger synthesizer") that combines latency, error rate, token cost, and throughput signals into a single probabilistic rollback trigger. The synthesizer must be cohort-aware (per-customer, per-model-version), support configurable hysteresis to avoid flapping, and expose tuning knobs in the Console.

Scope:
- Combine multiple SLO signals (p95 latency, p99 latency, 5xx error rate, token cost per request, sustainable throughput) into a unified score.
- Use temporal smoothing (EWMA) and Bayesian posterior checks to reduce false positives from short spikes.
- Implement cohort baselining: compute expected baselines per customer/route and only evaluate relative deviations when baselines are stable.
- Provide adaptive threshold scheduling: derive thresholds from historical variance and allow manual overrides.
- Surface synthetic trigger score and contributing signal breakdown in Console and Alerts.
- Provide backtesting harness and simulated traffic runs to validate tuning.

Design notes:
- Signal normalization: each metric is transformed into a unitless deviation z_i = (observed - baseline)/sigma_baseline, then clipped and weighted by signal importance.
- Aggregation: final trigger score S = softmax_weighted_sum(z_i, w_i) with optional percentile anchoring (e.g., use 90th percentile of recent S samples).
- Decision logic: if posterior(P(S > T)) > alpha for window W, mark trigger=fire. Alpha and W are configurable per rollout.
- Hysteresis: maintain separate enter/exit thresholds (T_enter, T_exit) and minimum dwell time to prevent rapid toggles.
- Throughput interplay: when throughput drops due to external factors, give precedence to error/latency signals; when throughput increases, enforce stricter cost/latency signals.
- Safety: default conservative weights for cost signal to avoid rollbacks purely for token cost during short-lived spikes.

Integration points:
- Runtime: expose a light-weight feedback hook for the serving runtime to emit pre-aggregated metrics (per-request latency, error flag, token count).
- Console: Dashboard panel showing S time series, per-signal contributions, and throttle recommendations.
- Rollout engine: the trigger emits a deterministic boolean and an explainable payload consumed by the rollout controller to scale down/evacuate traffic.

Backtesting & simulation: include a synthetic workload generator that replays traffic with injected spikes for each SLO type and evaluates precision/recall of rollback decisions. Attach simulation artifacts and summary CSVs.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: overfitting thresholds to historical traffic patterns. Mitigation: use rolling windows and percentile thresholds, require minimum sample counts.
- Risk: signal noise for low-traffic cohorts. Mitigation: fall back to global baselines when cohort sample size < N_min.
- Risk: cost-driven oscillation. Mitigation: weight token-cost lower by default and require multi-window confirmation.
acceptance_criteria: Trigger synthesizer computes a single score S every 30s for each rollout cohort and persists the history to metrics store.
Console shows S, per-signal z-scores, and the current enter/exit thresholds for any active rollout.
Backtesting harness achieves >90% precision and >80% recall on a library of synthetic spike scenarios for latency and error signals.
Rollout controller responds to a fired trigger by reducing canary traffic according to existing rollback policy; no flapping observed in a 2-hour stress test.
Operators can override weights and thresholds via Console and changes are audited in the rollout history.
Performance: synthesizer adds <5ms p50 CPU overhead per request aggregation node under typical load and scales horizontally.

notes: Design trade-off: Bayesian checks reduce false positives but require selecting priors; we pick weakly informative priors and expose tuning.
We discussed a ML approach (classifier over raw signals) but deferred to deterministic, explainable scoring for initial launch.
Consider adding a cost-savings mode that relaxes latency thresholds during off-peak hours — tracked as a follow-up.
Related ticket ENG-34120 contains cohort baselining utilities; reuse its baseline store APIs.
Console UX should allow applying temporary 'shelve' periods where triggers are ignored for planned experiments.
